builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Continual Classification Beyond the Kernel Regime: Harnessing the Sparsity Bias of L2 Regularization in Diagonal Linear Networks
summary: Replaces conventional L2 or L1 regularization centered on previous-task weights in continual linear/diagonal-network classification with a weighted L2 variant designed to preserve the sparsity bias of deep linear models. Costs are limited to implementing the per-weight weighting and accepting some long-horizon bias relative to standard continual L2. Can fail if the underlying teacher is not sufficiently sparse, since the claimed speed and accuracy advantage depends on that sparsity.
rationale: The method is cheap to implement in a constrained setup, but its benefit is conditional on a sparse-teacher assumption, so workload-specific validation is warranted before production adoption.
technique: Weighted L2 regularization for continual classification

claims.statement: Replaces conventional L2 or L1 regularization centered on previous-task weights in continual linear/diagonal-network classification with a weighted L2 variant designed to preserve the sparsity bias of deep linear models. Costs are limited to implementing the per-weight weighting and accepting some long-horizon bias relative to standard continual L2. Can fail if the underlying teacher is not sufficiently sparse, since the claimed speed and accuracy advantage depends on that sparsity.

For a sufficiently sparse teacher, converges substantially faster than directly learning a linear predictor with conventional continual L2 or L1 regularization, trading some long-horizon bias for markedly improved performance over moderate task horizons.
